- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward surprise.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to over-predict early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 2–5%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 patterns, model often misaligns with true trend; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.
